highlights: Vihara with elaborate paintings including Bodhisattva Padmapani and Bodhisattva Vajrapani. Well-preserved murals showing court scenes and Jataka tales.
visit_info: One of the finest painted caves; allow 15-20 minutes for detailed viewing.

highlights: Large vihara known for exceptional ceiling paintings including geometric and floral patterns. Features paintings of Hariti (goddess of fertility) and other Buddhist deities.
visit_info: Famous for ceiling art and wall paintings; plan 15-20 minutes.

highlights: Early chaitya hall (prayer hall) with stupa. Simple and austere design from the Hinayana phase. Horseshoe-shaped arch entrance.
visit_info: One of the oldest caves; architectural significance; 10 minutes.

highlights: The earliest cave at Ajanta. Chaitya hall with octagonal columns and a votive stupa at the rear. Inscriptions from later periods on the walls.
visit_info: Historically the oldest dated cave; 10 minutes for viewing.

highlights: Vihara with famous 'Dying Princess' mural (Sundari fainting upon hearing of Nanda's renunciation). Large hall with elaborate carvings and paintings.
visit_info: Known for the emotional 'Dying Princess' scene; 15 minutes.

highlights: One of the most richly painted caves with numerous Jataka tales illustrated. Features the Wheel of Life, scenes from Buddha's life, and elaborate decorative motifs.
visit_info: Extensive paintings; best preserved murals; allow 20 minutes.

highlights: Ornate chaitya hall with elaborate facade featuring intricate carvings. Buddha figures in teaching posture, decorated columns and horseshoe window.
visit_info: Architecturally ornate; noted for detailed facade; 10-15 minutes.

highlights: Large chaitya hall with magnificent sculptures including a reclining Buddha in parinirvana (death) position. Elaborate pillars and detailed narrative panels.
visit_info: Notable for parinirvana sculpture and grand scale; 15-20 minutes.

highlights: Large vihara with two rows of benches running the length of the hall, suggesting it may have been used as a dining hall. Simple but spacious design.
visit_info: Unique dining hall layout; 10 minutes.

highlights: Vishvakarma Cave or 'Carpenter's Cave' - chaitya hall with vaulted ceiling resembling wooden architecture. Large Buddha statue in preaching pose.
visit_info: Known as Carpenter's Cave; beautiful chaitya hall; 15 minutes.

highlights: Three-story vihara known as Tin Thal. Contains Buddha figures in teaching and meditation poses across multiple levels. Large monastery complex.
visit_info: Multi-story monastery structure; allow 15 minutes.

highlights: Ravana ki Khai cave. Features sculptures of Hindu deities including Durga, Vishnu, and Shiva. Marks the transition from Buddhist to Hindu caves.
visit_info: Transition period architecture; 10 minutes.

highlights: Dashavatara Cave featuring the ten avatars of Vishnu. Two-story structure with elaborate carvings of Shiva and Vishnu legends.
visit_info: Rich sculptural narrative; notable Shiva panels; 15 minutes.

highlights: The Kailasa Temple - monolithic temple carved from top down out of a single rock. Dedicated to Shiva, it represents Mount Kailash. Features intricate sculptures of gods, goddesses, and mythological scenes across multiple levels. Considered one of the most remarkable rock-cut structures in the world.
visit_info: UNESCO highlight; allow 45-60 minutes for full exploration. Must-see.

highlights: Rameshvara Cave with elegant sculptures of river goddesses Ganga and Yamuna at entrance. Features fine carvings of Shiva, Parvati, and attendants.
visit_info: Known for graceful goddess sculptures; 10-15 minutes.

highlights: Dhumar Lena cave similar in plan to Elephanta caves. Features large sculptures of Shiva including Shiva slaying demon Andhaka. Cross-shaped plan with shrines.
visit_info: Elephanta-style layout; Shiva legends; 10 minutes.

highlights: Chhota Kailash (Small Kailash) - Jain cave resembling the Kailasa temple in layout but smaller. Dedicated to Jain Tirthankaras. Incomplete due to rock flaws.
visit_info: Miniature Kailasa design; 10 minutes.

highlights: Indra Sabha (Assembly Hall of Indra) - elaborate two-story Jain temple with a monolithic shrine. Features intricate carvings of Jain Tirthankaras, lotus ceiling, and Ambika (Yakshi) sculpture.
visit_info: Most ornate Jain cave; allow 15-20 minutes.

highlights: Jagannatha Sabha with detailed carvings of Mahavira and other Tirthankaras. Features a central shrine and elaborate pillars with floral motifs.
visit_info: Detailed Jain iconography; 10 minutes.

highlights: Small Jain cave with a single-story layout. Contains sculptures of Tirthankaras and guardian figures. Relatively simple compared to nearby Jain caves.
visit_info: Smaller Jain shrine; 5-10 minutes.
